_comment: Map 2, marble: the Bentham drawing in the Temple of Time's stone, one closed rotunda authored in WORLD coordinates -- instance at identity. The ground floor at y -1.0 is covered in marble spikes; the running lane is a gallery walkway slab r 46.7..59.55 at y 23.0 (Map 1's ring height) with its inner edge OPEN over a 24 m drop to the spikes; the wall is seven tiers of 64 arched cells (448 cells, 4.0 x 5.5 m mouths, 3.0 m deep, five iron bars over every arch), three tiers below the walkway and four above, a pilaster on every pier, a cornice on every tier, a Greek-key frieze at 55.0..56.8, a great cornice, and a solid RIBBED dome from y 57.8 to the crown at 84.8 -- the Bentham drawing's own pattern: a smooth collar off the great cornice to a ring moulding, sixteen broad meridional ribs 0.85 m proud converging on the flat medallion r 4.2, and between them SMOOTH panels wearing the drawing's band of pointed flutes PAINTED (Ryan: "only the triangles ... they just painted on the roof") through one 128 x 64 px sheet of the atlas, one panel, unwrapped per face from azimuth and latitude. No oculus. ONE material: the painted 256 px atlas (USE_TEXTURE_FILES swaps in textures/marble_albedo.png). MarbleCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node: the floor, the slab (top, inner face, underside), the plain wall face, the dome. The spikes and bars are NOT colliders -- the scene's kill cylinder kills a body before it lands. Godot turns the collider into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn. The stone is 82,688 triangles and the collider 2,304: seven tiers of barred cells is what the drawing costs, the 2,240 cell bars (straight square prisms, 10 triangles each, 22,400) most of it; the dome is 2,240 (was 3,424 with the flutes modelled). max_tris is the audit's own tris= line, stone AND collider together (lib/glb_audit.py gates on that one number): 84,992 today, 85,500 the ceiling.
